title: Transition to chaos in two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection: the role of the magnetic field
authors: Francis F. Franco, Gabriel de T. Paula, Roman Chertovskih, Dalton N. Oliveira, Erico L. Rempel
abstract: The impact of an externally imposed magnetic field on numerical simulations of two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection (RBC) is investigated. Initially, the RBC model is examined in the absence of a magnetic field to establish a baseline. Then, a background magnetic field is introduced, and its influence on the transition to chaos is explored. For the purely hydrodynamic case and a range of the reduced Rayleigh number, the system exhibits traveling rolls which, after an attractor-merging crisis, give way to chaotic traveling rolls. Upon imposing a background magnetic field, there is a notable increase in the occurrence of traveling roll dynamics. Furthermore, the presence of the magnetic field favors the splitting/breaking of convective rolls, indicating a possible mechanism for transition to two-dimensional turbulence, with the structure of the convection cell being disrupted. A detailed analysis of the velocity field reveals that the collision between a saddle point and the center of a convective roll restores the system's original topology, with two symmetric kinetic vortices. During this collision, a magnetic vortex splits in two as a result of a magnetic reconnection. This behavior occurs intermittently in time.
summary: This work numerically investigates magnetoconvection in 2D Rayleigh-Bénard convection to understand the role of an external magnetic field on the transition to chaos. The key finding is that the magnetic field enhances chaotic roll behavior and facilitates vortex splitting through magnetic reconnection events during flow instabilities. This provides a detailed, non-linear fluid dynamics model for understanding turbulence onset.
main_problem: The study investigates how an externally imposed magnetic field influences the transition from ordered convective flow to chaos in two-dimensional Rayleigh-Bénard convection (RBC). It specifically examines the role of this magnetic field on the onset and nature of turbulent behavior.
main_result: Introducing a background magnetic field increases chaotic traveling roll dynamics and promotes the breaking/splitting of convective rolls, suggesting a mechanism for transitioning to 2D turbulence. This process is linked to intermittent magnetic vortex splitting via reconnection during saddle-roll interactions.
method: The analysis relies on numerical simulations using pseudospectral methods to solve non-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic equations. Diagnostics include Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponents (FTLE), Instantaneous Vorticity Deviation (IVD), and Local Current Deviation (LCD).
model_or_system: The system is two-dimensional, incompressible, electrically conducting fluid undergoing Rayleigh-Bénard convection under the influence of a uniform background magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}_0$). The dynamics are governed by modified Boussinesq approximations.
key_observables: Traveling rolls dynamics, chaotic behavior, vortex structures (kinetic and magnetic), bifurcation points, and reconnection events.
important_parameters: Reduced Rayleigh number ($r$), Chandrasekhar number ($Q$, related to $\mathbf{B}_0$), Prandtl number ($Pr$), and magnetic Prandtl number ($Pm$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to a two-dimensional formulation, which simplifies the study of topological dynamics compared to full 3D MHD turbulence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate velocity IVD and magnetic LCD alongside streamlines at specific times, highlighting saddle point/roll interactions and non-colliding vortex structures during reconnection events.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the baseline chaotic transition in the purely hydrodynamic case ($Q=0$). It then systematically introduces $\mathbf{B}_0$ ($Q>0$), analyzing how this field alters the dynamics, promoting roll breaking and detailing the topological changes associated with magnetic reconnection during flow interactions.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics (MHD), the study of pattern formation, chaos transition routes (e.g., crisis mechanisms), and localized energy dissipation/reconnection events shares mathematical parallels with non-equilibrium quantum field theories or open quantum systems exhibiting complex dynamics.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Test of numerical resolution. The time series of the kinetic energy is shown for three different resolutions and different choices of r and Q, as indicated in each panel.

Fig. 2. Bifurcation diagram for |ω101| as a function of r. Blue diamonds represent fixed point attractors, red circles denote periodic attractors, purple circles are periodic traveling rolls, green circles are quasiperiodic attractors, and magenta squares represent chaotic attractors.

Fig. 3. Phase space projection on Im(ω101) × Re(ω101). (a) five symmetric periodic attractors: AaP R (blue), AbP R (black), AcP R (magenta), A1P R (red) and A2P R (green) at r = 219. The gray area represents a non-attracting periodic traveling roll set. In (b) and (e), the power spectra for the time series of Re(ω101) are shown for r = 219 and r = 220, respectively. (d) Periodic traveling roll attractor AP T R for r = 220. Figures (c) and (f) are enlargements of the box regions in (a) and (d), respectively.

Fig. 4. Time series of the real part of the highest energy mode of vorticity ω101 for r = 219 and r = 220, in (a) and (b), respectively. In (a) is shown the long initial transient before convergence to the periodic attractor AP R b . In (b), the time series corresponds to the periodic traveling roll attractor AP T R. This initial transient in (a) is constituted by a non-attracting periodic traveling roll.
